public class Robot extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.TimedRobot
Top-level robot class. This is instantiated by the WPILib runtime once and is responsible for handing control to the CommandScheduler every loop cycle, managing match phase transitions, and logging infrastructure.

TimedRobot calls the appropriate Init, Periodic, and Exit methods based on the current Driver Station mode. The 20 ms robot loop frequency is set by WPILib â€” do not add blocking calls anywhere in this class.

  • Constructor Details

    • Robot

      public Robot()
      Robot constructor â€” runs once on power-on before any mode is enabled.
      • DataLogManager.start() opens a .wpilog binary file on the roboRIO (/home/lvuser/logs/) or a USB drive (/u/logs/) and automatically captures every NetworkTables key change to it. The Driver Station copies these files to the operator laptop after each match.
      • DataLogManager.logConsoleOutput(boolean) routes System.out into the same .wpilog so error messages appear in AdvantageScope's Console tab.
      • PortForwarder tunnels PhotonVision's HTTP dashboard (port 5800) through the robot radio so it remains accessible from the Driver Station laptop.
      • The health timer is started here so robotPeriodic() can begin rate-limiting immediately.

  • Method Details

    • robotPeriodic

      public void robotPeriodic()
      Runs every 20 ms regardless of mode. Drives the WPILib command scheduler and the robot state machine, then publishes system-health metrics at 10 Hz.

      Health metrics (battery voltage, CAN utilization, RSL state) are rate-limited to 10 Hz because they are slow-moving signals; writing them every 20 ms would waste NT4 bandwidth and contributed to loop overruns before Stage 0 optimizations.

    • teleopPeriodic

      public void teleopPeriodic()
      Reads the FMS game-specific message once per teleop period to determine which scoring windows are active for each alliance.

      The game-specific message is a string set by the FMS (or the Driver Station in practice mode). The first character encodes the hub color that the other team is targeting:

      • 'R' â€” the opposing alliance is targeting the Red hub.
      • 'B' â€” the opposing alliance is targeting the Blue hub.

      This robot sets its own state based on whether the hub color matches its alliance:

      • If the hub color matches this robot's alliance (e.g., Blue bot + Blue hub), the robot is set INACTIVE â€” it is not supposed to shoot into its own hub at that moment.
      • If the hub color does NOT match (e.g., Blue bot + Red hub), the robot is ACTIVE â€” it should shoot now.

      The hasData() guard ensures this logic runs only once; subsequent calls are no-ops once the message has been received and cached.

      Overrides:
      teleopPeriodic in class edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.IterativeRobotBase
